subject: Request: transition notice template & objection timeline for subprocessor changes
messages:
From: Emma Lambert <emma_lambert@vendorco.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: matthew.harris@clearbank.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: shorten subprocessor notification window (DPA redline attached)

Hi Tessa,

Quick note from VendorCo legal — we have a customer (ClearBank) asking for a tighter operational cadence around subprocessor changes. They want the notification window reduced to 15 days for non-critical changes and a 10-day objection window; we understand Redwood's standard is 30/30.

I've attached our suggested redline to the subprocessor notification section to show the specific wording (Vendor_Redline_Subprocessor_Notice_20260801.docx). Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept a 15-day notify / 10-day objection timeline for non-elevated processors? For critical processors (KMS, hosting), we propose the existing 30/30 remains.

If helpful, we can jump on a short call — cc'ing Matthew from ClearBank who asked for the change.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lambert
Legal Operations, VendorCo
attachment: Vendor_Redline_Subprocessor_Notice_20260801.docx (word/docx, 44KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lambert <emma_lambert@vendorco.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, matthew.harris@clearbank.com
Date: 2026-08-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: shorten subprocessor notification window (DPA redline attached)

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and for sending a redline.

Two quick items: 1) we need Legal to weigh in on whether a 15/10 split preserves our ability to object and remediate (looping in Karthik), and 2) we need to confirm operationally how that would be implemented in our console and in our monthly subprocessor CSV exports (looping in Laura).

Karthik / Laura — can you review Emma's suggested language and confirm whether Redwood can accept: 15 days notice / 10 days objection for non-critical processors, with an explicit carve-out retaining 30/30 for security-critical processors (KMS, infra, logging)? If we can accept this, I'd like to route the DPA redline via DocuSign rather than a protracted exec cycle.

Emma / Matthew — rough timeline from our side: Legal review today, and if approved we can issue counterparty redline tomorrow and circulate a DocuSign for signatures within 48 hours.

-Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Emma Lambert <emma_lambert@vendorco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, matthew.harris@clearbank.com
Date: 2026-08-02T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: shorten subprocessor notification window (DPA redline attached)

Thanks for the ping, Tessa. Reviewed the vendor redline. Summary of Redwood's position:

- We're open to reducing the notice period for non-critical processors, but the objection window must allow sufficient time for technical validation and, if necessary, to implement mitigations or an alternative routing. 10 days is tight.
- Proposed compromise language (high level): 15 days notice / 20 days objection for non-critical processors; 30 days notice / 30 days objection for security-critical processors. We also include an expedited escalation process for high-severity security concerns.
- Require explicit definitions in the DPA appendix for "security-critical processors" with examples (KMS, persistent storage hosting, logging/telemetry ingest).

I've attached the counter redline (DPA_Redline_v3.docx) with inline language. Key additions:
1) Section 4.2(a) — definitions and examples for critical processors.
2) Section 4.2(b) — 15/20 carve for non-critical and retention of 30/30 for critical.
3) Section 4.2(c) — an objection escalation ladder that requires good-faith technical evidence to trigger an expedited 7-day review for critical issues.

Operational ask for Laura: If we accept 15/20, can your infra team ensure the notification is surfaced within the customer console and that the monthly Subprocessor_List CSV includes a "pending change" flag so customers have machine-readable notice?

If Emma and ClearBank accept the 15/20 compromise, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and route it through our standard legal signature flow.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachment: DPA_Redline_v3.docx (word/docx, 86KB)

From: Emma Lambert <emma_lambert@vendorco.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Harris <matthew.harris@clearbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: shorten subprocessor notification window (DPA redline attached)

Karthik — appreciate the clear framing and the counter proposal. ClearBank is comfortable with the 15/20 compromise for non-critical processors and keeping 30/30 for critical ones. The proposed expedited 7-day ladder for high-severity items is acceptable provided it's narrowly scoped.

We'll accept Redwood's DPA_Redline_v3.docx and are ready to sign via DocuSign. Please send the envelope.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning?docId=abc123def

Matthew — thanks for coordinating on ClearBank's side. If there are any internal approvals needed on your end, please flag them.

Thanks — Emma

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lambert <emma_lambert@vendorco.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, matthew.harris@clearbank.com
Date: 2026-08-03T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: shorten subprocessor notification window (DPA redline attached)

Great — thanks everyone. Final notes and next steps:

- We will proceed with the 15 days notice / 20 days objection for non-critical processors, retain 30/30 for security-critical processors, and include the 7-day expedited ladder only for narrowly-defined high-severity incidents.
- Legal will publish the executed DPA via DocuSign and attach the finalized Appendix A (Subprocessor list). Laura's team will attach the current Subprocessor_List_20260801.csv that includes the "pending change" flag for any upcoming transitions.
- Action items:
  * Karthik: please route the DPA_Redline_v3.docx to our DocuSign admin and set signing order to Redwood (legal) -> VendorCo -> ClearBank.
  * Laura: confirm the CSV export contains the pending-change field and share the file.
  * Emma: sign the DocuSign envelope when it arrives.

I'll mark this thread as the single source for the execution steps; please update if anything deviates.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
